old_title: Israel plane hijacking live: Attacker shouted 'kill me' after passengers intervened
new_title: Israel flight hijacking live: New footage emerges after 'pilot attacked with axe'

The attacker who tried to hijack a flydubai flightwas "clearly suicidal" and shouted "kill me" after being subdued by passengers and crew, Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said.
"It's clear he was suicidal, that's not a question," he added.
Netanyahu also said the co-pilot, who Israel says was Omani, had undergone "Islamist radical indoctrination".
It comes as he United Arab Emirates has launched an investigation into whether the flydubai flight hijacking was linked to terrorism, after the failed attempted to crash the plane on Wednesday morning.
The Flydubai Flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Israel dramatically descended approximately 13,000 feet in 30 seconds during the chaos on Wednesday morning.
UAE investigators will now determine "whether the incident was linked to any terrorist activity or purpose, or involved prior planning or direction", according to the UAE's state news agency.
Abu Dhabi authorities have jurisdiction over the incident because the aircraft is registered in the UAE and flies under its flag, the statement said.
Netanyahu earlier named the Indian pilot who was stabbed during the attempted hijacking, calling him a "true hero".
Israel believes arrested co-pilot was acting alone - Reuters
Israeli officials believe the co-pilot, who was arrested by Saudi authorities, was acting alone when he attempted to crash the flydubai plane on Wednesday.
It comes after Israel's envoy to the UAE, Yossi Shelley, said the suspect was an Omani national.
Attacker was suicidal and shouting 'kill me' after being subdued, says Netanyahu
The attacker behind the attempt to hijack a flydubai flight was suicidal and appeared to have been attempting to down the plane, Benjamin Netanyahu said.
The attacker was shouting "kill me, kill me" after he was subdued and tied up using phone cables, the Israeli president added.
"It's clear he was suicidal, that's not a question," he added.
Netanyahu also said the co-pilot had undergone a radical Islamist indoctrination.
Israel will be able to say within a matter of days whether the co-pilot had connections to Iran, he said.
Netanyahu: Co-pilot had undergone a radical Islamist indoctrination
We've just heard more from Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who was speaking to Fox News' Fox and Friends programme on Thursday morning US time.
He said the co-pilot of the flydubai flight had undergone a radical indoctrination.
"We know that he underwent Islamist radical indoctrination," Netanyahu said in an interview with Fox News.
Trump calls co-pilot who tried to hijack Israel flight 'a terrorist or a whack job'
President Donald Trump has said a co-pilot who stabbed his colleague during a flight to Israel was "a terrorist or a whack-job."
The commander-in-chief made the remarks Wednesday, after the attempted hijacking of a Flydubai flight headed to Tel Aviv. The co-pilot, who was arrested when the plane landed, was subdued by passengers who described what happened during the terrifying ordeal as the bloody scene unfolded.
Speaking in the Oval Office, Trump told reporters he had spoken about the incident with Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu.
"I did speak to Bibi Netanyahu at length about this event, and it seems as though the co-pilot was perhaps a terrorist or perhaps a whack-job, and he stabbed the pilot," Trump remarked.
The president was also asked whether he knew if the co-pilot had wanted to crash the jet.
'The plane felt like a rollercoaster as it nosedived'
We've just heard from another one of the passengers on the flydubai plane, Almog Italy, who revealed his dramatic experience to Sky News.
He said the plane felt like a "rollercoaster" as it initially dropped by around 13,000 feet in just 30 seconds.
"In the beginning, we didn't understand what was going on because we saw people rushing and also the crew members rushing to the front of the plane," he told the broadcaster.
"After three, four minutes, we understood that there was a kind of attack."
He said word soon spread about a stabbing in the cockpit, with the plane's passengers "afraid" but remaining calm.
Saudi Arabia refused Israeli requests to send planes to pick up passengers
Saudi Arabia turned down requests by Israel to send its own planes to pick up stranded passengers on Wednesday, a source has told AFP news agency.
Israeli passengers on the diverted flydubai flight were stranded in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.
FlyDubai: The airline that made an emergency landing after a captain was stabbed
A copilot on a flight to Israel stabbed a captain on Wednesday before passengers pushed their way into the cockpit and wrestled with the attacker.
The FlyDubai plane fell rapidly, with a passenger saying he grabbed the controls and pulled upward, similar to how he had seen on television.
Other crew members soon took over, and the jetliner made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.
It was not clear what motivated the attack. Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu said that Saudi Arabia had arrested the copilot.
The passengers from the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv were greeted with cheers in Israel as they completed the journey on another flight Wednesday evening.
Here we take a look at the airline in which the altercation took place.
Four Americans were aboard Israel-bound plane: reports
Four Americans were aboard the Israel-bound plane that a pilot allegedly attempted to hijack Wednesday, according to reports.
The four passengers on the Flydubai flight were US-Israeli dual citizens, US officials told CNN and NewsNation.

New footage shows chaotic scenes aboard a FlyDubai flight to Israel as passengers wrestled a man who attacked his co-pilot with an axe in a suspected hijacking.
Terrified people on the flight are seen speaking in a mixture of Hebrew and English as they call for a doctor and a pilot. Others shout "take him out" and "he tried to crash the plane" in the video shared by Israel's Channel 12 news.
The co-pilot who allegedly tried to hijack a flight to Israel on Wednesday attacked his fellow pilot with an axe, Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu claimed as questions loomed over the motives and background of the assailant.
It remains unclear how the pilot gained access to a weapon and some analysts have suggested it may have been the emergency axe kept in the cockpit in case of emergency.
Passenger Daniel Schlichter told Fox News on Thursday that the cabin was alerted to the attack by a woman and her daughter who saw the incident while heading to the lavatory.
Off-duty British pilot 'helped rescue plane' after alleged stabbing in cockpit
An off-duty British pilot helped rescue a passenger flight from Dubai to Israel after a pilot allegedly stabbed his colleague and tried to hijack the plane, a passenger has said.
The FlyDubai plane dropped from 33,000 feet to 17,000 feet (10,000 metres to 5,100 metres) in about a minute as passengers and crew subdued the alleged attacker.
Dozens of Omani pilots flew to Tel Aviv despite ban, says report
A ban on pilots from states without formal relations to Israel was not enforced appropriately, according to a report cited by the Times of Israel.
Under the law, pilots from nations including Oman, which does not have formal ties with Israel, were banned from flying but airlines and security agencies did not enforce the rule.
It comes as an unnamed Omani national was said to have attacked his Indian co-pilot on a FlyDubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv.
Air travel expert gives verdict on three key issues of the Flydubai plane hijacking
The alleged hijacking of an Israel-bound flight has raised questions over how secure the vetting process is for one of aviation's most skilled jobs.
Flydubai FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv rapidly descended during a terrifying ordeal as the co-pilot allegedly tried to take control of the plane after attacking his fellow pilot with an axe, or possibly stabbing him.
Watch: New footage shows bloodied Flydubai passengers rush to subdue pilot
Israel's Shin Bet had security concerns about UAE airports weeks before hijacking attempt: report
The head of Israel's security agency had raised security concerns about flights from the UAE for months before a pilot attempted to hijack a Flydubai passenger plane travelling to Tel Aviv, according to a report.
David Zini, the director of Israel's Shin Bet, had reportedly clashed with Israeli airlines over restrictions on flights to the UAE, with the agency reasoning that security measures at Emirati airports were insufficient, according to Israel's N12 News.
Israeli authorities were concerned with possible missile attacks or attacks at an airport, the outlet reported on Thursday. A scenario like Wednesday's hijacking attempt was "not raised in any discussion", they said.
Trump warns Tehran would be 'hit very hard' if FlyDubai attack linked to Iran
US president Donald Trump has warned that Iran would be "hit very hard" if it was found to have been involved in the attack.
Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu said pilots from countries without diplomatic relations with Israel were generally barred from flying there, raising questions over how the suspected Omani pilot was allowed on the Flydubai flight.
He said: "Obviously there was a loophole here and we're taking care of that among other things... with the full co-operation, I have to say, of the Emirati government, so we're both interested in making sure this doesn't happen again."
Oman, unlike the UAE, does not have formal diplomatic ties with Israel.
Asked whether there was evidence of Iranian involvement, Netanyahu said: "It's too early to say."
Watch: Flydubai pilot reveals desperate attempts to unlock cockpit to passengers while being attacked
Flydubai pilot tells India PM Modi he opened cockpit door while being attacked
An Indian pilot who was attacked in the FlyDubai flight incident told prime minister Narendra Nodi on Wednesday that he opened the door of the plane's cockpit while being attacked, according to a video clip released by the prime minister's office on Friday.
Watch: Netanyahu says Flydubai co-pilot underwent Islamist radical indoctrination
Israeli defence minister claims Flydubai cockpit attack 'jihadist terror attack'
Israeli defence minister Israel Katz has described the Flydubai cockpit incident as "a jihadist terrorist attack attempt".
Katz said in a statement: "The grave incident on the flydubai plane was a jihadist terrorist attack attempt, which was thwarted only thanks to the bravery of several Israeli passengers who broke into the cockpit, overpowered the terrorist and, with their own hands, restored control of the plane to another flight crew who was present there."
Israel's ambassador to the UN Danny Danon said that there was "no doubt" the pilot intended to bring the Tel Aviv-bound plane down.
"We have no doubt that it was a terror attack from a radical individual. We still cannot link it to a terror state or a terror organisation, but for sure we know that there was an intention to bring that plane down," he told Fox News.
He also described the incident as an attack on the Abraham Accords.
